Whereas the Town of Ajax values active living, recreation, and sport as key contributors to community health and quality of life for residents of all ages; and, Whereas the Town offers a variety of soccer-related opportunities and assets for residents, including both grass and artificial turf fields, as well as portable soccer net frames available for both community and organization use; and, Whereas residents and groups may apply for permits to use the Town's artificial turf fields, located at the Ajax Community Centre, known as Monarch Field and Centennial Field, which provide consistent playing conditions and resilience to weather compared to natural grass surfaces, making them a valuable recreational asset; and, Whereas residents have expressed interest in greater clarity around the Town's approach to soccer netting, turf field access, and potential opportunities for informal or drop in use of artificial turf fields when not otherwise booked. Therefore, be it resolved: That Ajax Council directs Operations and Environmental Services staff to prepare a report by June 2026, outlining the Town of Ajax's current position on the installation of soccer netting on municipal soccer fields, an overview of the Town's turf field booking and permitting process, as well as a high-level scan of how other comparable municipalities manage access to artificial turf fields, and feasibility, risks, and operational implications allowing public use of artificial turf fields during unbooked periods.

item: 10.4 Criminal Exploitation of Minors for Organized Crime
text: Whereas organized theft, vehicle tracking, and related criminal activities are increasing across Ontario communities, placing residents, businesses, and vulnerable youth at heightened risk; and, Whereas police services and community advocates have identified a troubling pattern of adults recruiting, coercing, or manipulating minors into participating in OT (“out of town”) activities, including tracking, surveillance, transportation of stolen goods, and organized retail theft; and, Whereas this pattern is directly connected to the broader crisis highlighted in Missing Black Boys, where vulnerable youth, particularly Black youth, are targeted, isolated, exploited, and placed in situations of significant danger; and, Whereas Bill C-14 strengthens bail and sentencing provisions for violent and organized offences, including motor vehicle theft and extortion, but does not address the criminal exploitation of minors for organized property crime, nor does it create specific offences or aggravating factors for adults who involve youth in such activities; and, Whereas youth who are exploited by adults for OT tracking or organized theft may become key witnesses in criminal proceedings, and these minors face significant risks of retaliation, stigma, and public exposure if required to testify without enhanced privacy protections; and, Whereas current federal legislation does not explicitly guarantee closed court testimony, automatic publication bans, or YCJA equivalent privacy protections for minors who are witnesses, rather than offenders, in cases involving organized property crime or criminal exploitation; and, Whereas municipalities have a responsibility to advocate for community safety, youth protection, and upstream prevention, particularly where legislative gaps place vulnerable young people at risk. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That the Town of Ajax call on the Government of Canada to: a) Amend the Criminal Code to create a specific offence for adults who recruit, coerce, exploit, or use minors in organized theft, tracking, surveillance, or related criminal activities. b) Establish aggravating sentencing factors for any adult convicted of an offence involving the criminal exploitation of a minor in organized property crime. c) Expand reverse-onus bail provisions to include adults charged with offences involving the recruitment or exploitation of minors for organized theft or tracking. d) Strengthen federal legislation to ensure that minors who are exploited by adults and required to testify in criminal proceedings have access to: - Closed-court testimony - Automatic publication bans, and - Enhanced privacy protections equivalent to those provided under the Youth Criminal Justice Act. 2. That the Town of Ajax call on the Province of Ontario to: a) Increase funding and resources for police services to investigate organized theft, youth recruitment, and criminal exploitation. b) Expand youth prevention, diversion, and early-intervention programs in partnership with school boards, community agencies, and culturally specific organizations. c) Improve data collection, inter-agency coordination, and community-based supports to better identify and prevent youth recruitment into organized crime. 3. That this motion be circulated to all Durham Region municipalities, Durham Regional Police Services Board, Local Members of Parliament and Members of Provincial Parliament, The Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), The Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM), and Durham Region Council.

item: 10.5 Ethical Investment and Human Rights Due Diligence in Public Pension (Main Motion)
text: Whereas a recent investigation by environmental advocacy group Stand.earth found the Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System (OMERS), eight other public pensions, and all of Canada's major banks have invested in companies that provide services to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) through multimillion-dollar contracts; and, Whereas ICE operations have been widely criticized for human rights violations, including the detention of children and the disproportionate targeting of Black, Indigenous, Latino/a, and racialized communities; and, Whereas Ajax is home to many families with cross-border ties, migrant histories, and communities directly affected by U.S. immigration enforcement practices, making the investment decisions of Canadian banks and pension funds a matter of local interest; and, Whereas municipalities have a role in advocating for ethical governance and transparency in the investment of public funds. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That Ajax Council call on the federal government to establish ethical investment guidelines for federally regulated pension plans; and 2. That Ajax Council request the Province of Ontario to undertake a review of the Pension Benefits Act, Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System Act and relevant legislation to ensure an alignment with ethical investment frameworks and modern expectations of public accountability; and 3. Finance staff be directed to report back on the Town's procurement and responsible investment practices by June 2026; and 4. That a copy of this motion be circulated to the Hon. François-Philippe Champagne, Federal Minister of Finance, Jennifer McKelvie, MP for Ajax, local MPs across the Region of Durham, the Hon. Peter Bethlanfalvy, Ontario Minister of Finance, Rob Cerjanec, MPP for Ajax, local MPPs across the Region of Durham, and Durham Regional Council.

item: 10.6 Request for Operational Funding for Supportive and Transitional Housing
text: Whereas the Government of Canada has launched the Build Canada Homes (BCH) initiative to support the creation of new deeply affordable, supportive, and transitional housing through federal capital investments; and, Whereas the Town of Ajax is partnering with the Region of Durham to advance a 50 unit supportive housing development at the northeast corner of Harwood Avenue South and Achilles Road, a Regionally led project that is dependent on federal capital funding through Build Canada Homes; and, Whereas the Harwood and Achilles supportive housing project is designed to deliver long term, permanent housing with wrap around supports for individuals with complex needs, and its success is contingent on secure, ongoing operational funding to sustain services for residents; and, Whereas operational funding for rent supplements and wrap around supports, including health, mental health, social, and employment services, fall within areas of provincial responsibility; and, Whereas BCH requires applicants to address whether operational finances have been secured at the application stage and a provincial commitment is needed to unlock federal capital for the benefit of communities urgently seeking housing solutions. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That Ajax Council formally call on the Province of Ontario to commit the operational funding required to unlock federal capital for supportive and transitional housing projects through the Build Canada Homes program; and 2. That Ajax Council specifically urge the Province of Ontario to provide the operational funding necessary to support the 50 unit supportive housing development at Harwood Avenue South and Achilles Road in Ajax, being led by the Region of Durham; and 3. That a copy of this motion be circulated to Jennifer McKelvie, MP for Ajax, the Hon. Rob Flack, the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, the Hon. Michael Parsa, Minister of Children, Community and Social Services, the Hon. Sylvia Jones, Minister of Health, the Region of Durham, Rob Cerjanec, MPP for Ajax, the Region of Durham, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, and the Ontario Municipal Social Services Association.

Whereas, the Durham Meadoway Project is a proposal to implement a regional active transportation corridor and linear park extending from the City of Oshawa through to Rouge National Urban Park at the Pickering–Toronto boundary, including; and Whereas, in Ajax, the Meadoway as proposed would run adjacent to Taunton Road from the eastern border with Whitby to Westney Road, at which point it would follow the hydro corridor southwest through Paulynn Park including a portion along the Trans Canada Trail, to the Pickering border; and Whereas, Regional Council endorsed the Durham Meadoway Visioning Study in June 2024, and Region of Durham staff are proceeding with preliminary design work to advance the multi-use path and identify locations for gateways, amenities, and other features along the route; and Whereas, the cost-share arrangement outlined in the Shared Services Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to complete the preliminary design was determined by Regional Council and is proportionally allocated based on new infrastructure requirements within each municipality; and Whereas, the Town of Ajax's financial contribution toward the preliminary design work is $119,292, reflecting the extent of existing and future multi-use paths within the project area; and Whereas, any future detailed design and capital works or trail planning arising from the preliminary design study would be subject to Council approval through the Town's Capital Budget process. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That the Town of Ajax's financial contribution of $119,292 to Durham Region be funded from Development Charges and Development Reserve and costs be allocated to relevant capital projects.

item: 10.9 Funding Certainty for Organizations Supporting the Black Community
text: Whereas Durham Family and Cultural Centre (DFCC) is an Ajax-based charitable organization that provides a space for members of the Black community, and other racialized and diverse groups to engage in culturally focused programs such as counselling, parenting, education, mentorship, and child and youth development; and, Whereas the Town of Ajax is a highly diverse community, with approximately 65% of residents identifying as part of racialized or diverse groups, emphasizing the importance of culturally responsive services and support which are critical to the well-being and stability of Black and racialized families and serve as a source of meaningful employment within the local community; and, Whereas according to a letter received by DFCC from the Ministry of Citizenship and Multiculturalism, while the Government of Ontario has reaffirmed its support for the Black Youth Action Plan through an allocation of $16.6 million in the 2026-27 provincial budget, the province would not commit to ongoing or equivalent funding for previously funded organizations; and, Whereas the letter further stated that an update was expected to be provided to the affected agencies and organizations by early summer 2026; and Whereas, DFCC has stated that without the funding guarantee, they will be forced to immediately lay off 80% of their staff and reassess the programs they offer, which support 50 families and over 500 community members across Durham each year; and, Whereas organizations province-wide that support Black youth may be facing similar challenges as a result of funding uncertainty and such instability disproportionately impacts Black youth and their families. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That Ajax Council calls on the Province of Ontario to immediately commit to ongoing or equivalent funding for Durham Family and Cultural Centre (DFCC) for the 2026 budget year, in support of crucial programming for Black youth and families in Ajax and Durham Region; and 2. That Ajax Council further calls on the Province of Ontario to urgently provide clarity to DFCC and other organizations funded through the Ministry of Citizenship and Multiculturalism and provide better certainty to inform their fiscal planning; and 3. That a copy of this motion be circulated to the Hon. Graham McGregor, Minister of Citizenship and Multiculturalism; Dr. Parm Bhatthal, Assistant Deputy Minister of Citizenship and Multiculturalism; Rob Cerjanec, MPP for Ajax; John Henry, Durham Regional Chair; all lower tier Durham Region municipalities; and Debbie Miles-Senior, Executive Director of Durham Family and Cultural Centre.

item: 10.1 Reviewing the Ajax Municipal Flag Raising Policy
text: Whereas in September 2021, a community flagpole was installed at Pat Bayly Square to recognize special events, important days, public awareness campaigns, and Ajax's diverse population; and, Whereas Council granted the Clerk's department authority to approve such requests in line with the Town's Flag Raising Request Policy; and, Whereas the growing volume of flag raising requests has placed increasing strain on staff resources and has made it difficult to administer the program in a manner that is equitable for all members of the community; and Whereas the City of Toronto and the City of Mississauga have recently approved the exclusion of foreign national flags from being raised on their community flagpoles; and Whereas charitable and public awareness campaigns, and community celebrations and events will remain unaffected pending the completion of a comprehensive review of the Town's current Flag Raising Request Policy. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That Council directs Equity, Diversity and Inclusion staff to: a. amend the Flag Raising Request Policy (LIS-WI-026) to exclude the flying of flags representing foreign nations, perceived foreign nations and coalitions of foreign nations effective September 1, 2026; and b. undertake community consultation, in collaboration with relevant departments, to determine the continuation and curation of Town-hosted flag raising ceremonies that reflect the shared values of the Ajax community; and c. conduct a comprehensive policy review and report back to Council no later than the first quarter of 2027, with a Community Recognition Program proposal that addresses the Flag Raising Policy, the Ajax Sign Commemorative Lighting Program, proclamation requests, and community notification of ceremonies and significant days.

Therefore, be it resolved: That the Town of Ajax implement an additional fee of 15 per cent (15%) on all recreation memberships, ARC Performance Passes, Pay-Go, and Pay-Go 10 Passes, purchased by non residents, effective September 1, 2026.

item: 10.3 Supporting Ajax Pickering Road Watch Community Safety Initiatives

item: 4.1 Temporary Renaming of Pat Bayly Square for FIFA World Cup Celebrations
text: Whereas the Town of Ajax congratulates all teams participating in the 2026 FIFA World Cup and recognizes the global excitement, unity, and celebration that this tournament brings to communities around the world; and, Whereas many local fans will be gathering to cheer on their favourite teams during this international event, creating an opportunity for everyone to come together under the love of sport; and, Whereas the Town of Ajax is hosting upcoming Fan Zone Watch Parties on June 18 and June 24 at Pat Bayly Square, presented by Medallion Corporation, as part of local FIFA World Cup celebrations; and, Whereas Derek Cornelius, a member of Canada's Men's National Team, was born and raised in Ajax, attended local schools, and began his youth soccer journey with Ajax Soccer Club, reflecting the strong foundation that local sport and community support can provide; and, Whereas the Town of Ajax is immensely proud to see one of its own rise from the pitches of Ajax to soccer's grandest stage, inspiring young athletes across the community and bringing tremendous pride to residents as he represents Canada at the FIFA World Cup; and, Whereas Medallion Corporation has approached the Town with a desire to further celebrate community pride and enhance the public celebration through placemaking and commemorative activation tied to these events. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. Ajax Council approve the temporary renaming of Pat Bayly Square to Derek Cornelius Square, effective immediately, until the conclusion of the 2026 FIFA World Cup; and 2. A temporary public art installation recognizing Derek Cornelius and his connection to Ajax be unveiled at the June 18, 2026, Ajax Fan Zone Watch Party hosted in Derek Cornelius Square; and 3. The Business Engagement team, in coordination with Communications and Engagement staff, be directed to promote community awareness of this tribute; and 4. A copy of this motion be sent to Jennifer McKelvie, Member of Parliament for Ajax; Rob Cerjanec, Member of Provincial Parliament for Ajax; Durham Region Council; Medallion Corporation; and Ajax Soccer Club.

item: 10.1 Reducing Speed Limits on All Interior Roads to 40 km/h
text: Whereas the Highway Traffic Act establishes a default statutory speed limit of 50 km/h on municipal roads unless otherwise prescribed by by-law; and, Whereas municipalities across Ontario are increasingly adopting 40 km/h neighbourhood speed limits as a Vision Zero measure to reduce pedestrian injury severity, particularly for children, seniors, and persons with disabilities; and, Whereas Ajax continues to receive a high volume of resident concerns regarding speeding on local roads, particularly near parks, schools, and residential areas; and Whereas a modernized review is required to determine the feasibility, costs, operational impacts, and enforcement implications of adopting a 40 km/h speed limit on all interior roads in Ajax; and Whereas the recommendation to review the adoption of a 40 km/h neighbourhood speed limit originated from the June 4, 2026, Ajax-Pickering Road Watch Meeting and this motion has been reviewed and approved by their committee. Therefore, be it resolved: That Ajax Council directs Transportation Planning staff to prepare a report on the feasibility of reducing the speed limit on all local roads in the Town of Ajax to 40 km/h including signage requirements, cost estimates, a review of implementation models, options for phased implementation, any required amendments to existing town bylaws, and recommendations for next steps to be presented at the January 2027 Council Meeting.

item: 10.3 Advocating for Provincial Regulatory Modernization to Enable Access to
text: Whereas the Town of Ajax Accessibility Advisory Committee passed a motion at its May 20, 2026 meeting recommending Council to advocate for inclusion and equitable access to affordable assistive hearing technologies for all Ontarians; and, Whereas hearing loss affects millions of Ontarians and has significant impacts on communication, safety, employment, and quality of life; and Whereas, the Ontario Association of Professional Audiology Clinics (OAPAC) and Speech- Language & Audiology Canada (SAC) have stated that while lower-cost hearing support options can benefit consumers, individuals experiencing hearing loss should first consult a regulated audiologist, as symptoms may be caused by conditions ranging from wax build-up to more serious medical issues such as tumours, which consumer devices cannot diagnose; and Whereas, Apple and other technology manufacturers have developed low-risk assistive hearing features-such as sound amplification, personalized audio based on a user's hearing profile, and built-in hearing assessments-including Apple's Hearing Test and Hearing Aid features available on compatible AirPods devices that are enabled in many jurisdictions globally, allowing consumer devices like AirPods to function as assistive listening tools for adults 18 years of age and older with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss; and, Whereas on December 11, 2024, Health Canada issued Class II Medical Device Licences (MDLs) for Apple's Hearing Aid Feature and Hearing Test Feature, and by February 10, 2026, Apple's Medical Device Active Licence Listing (MDALL) included updated firmware and software components, confirming that the technology has received federal medical device authorization; and Whereas Health Canada's approval confirms that the devices meet applicable federal medical device safety, manufacturing, and quality-control standards, but Canada currently lacks a fully implemented access framework specific to over- the-counter (OTC) hearing aids, and access to hearing devices remains subject to provincial and territorial rules; and Whereas Ontario's current regulatory and dispensing framework for hearing devices does not clearly accommodate the OTC, user-controlled model of federally authorized, consumer-grade hearing and assistive listening features; and Whereas the Province of Ontario has launched consultation on allowing the sale and use of certain over-the-counter hearing aids, creating a timely opportunity for municipalities to advocate for a safe, accessible, and modern provincial pathway; and Whereas Apple currently states that the Hearing Test and Hearing Aid features are unavailable in Canada due to regulatory restrictions, despite the technology having received Health Canada medical device authorization; and Whereas emerging technologies such as software-enabled hearing aid and assistive listening features have the potential to significantly improve accessibility in public and private spaces, yet major device manufacturers have not enabled this functionality on widely used devices in Ontario due to regulatory restrictions and uncertainty; and Whereas without provincial modernization, Ontario risks falling behind global accessibility standards, limiting access to affordable assistive listening tools and hindering progress toward inclusive environments. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That the Town of Ajax formally requests that the Province of Ontario, specifically the Minister of Health and the Minister for Seniors and Accessibility, expedite and complete its current review of provincial regulations governing hearing-related technologies, with the goal of establishing a clear pathway for enabling federally authorized, low-risk, over- the-counter hearing aid and assistive listening features embedded in consumer devices. This review should include consideration of: a. A clear provincial access pathway for federally authorized, low-risk OTC hearing aid and assistive listening features, including software-enabled features embedded in consumer devices. b. Alignment with federal approvals already granted by Health Canada. c. Global standards and practices in jurisdictions where these features are already enabled. d. Safeguards that ensure users are encouraged to seek professional assessment when experiencing hearing loss, especially where symptoms are sudden, severe, one-sided, associated with pain, dizziness, drainage, or other medical concerns. e. Functional safety requirements including output limits, performance standards, user warnings, age restrictions, and consumer protection requirements. 2. That the Province of Ontario provide clear written guidance to manufacturers, platform providers, hearing care professionals, municipalities, and the public on the conditions under which federally authorized OTC hearing aid and assistive listening features may be enabled and used in Ontario. 3. That for this review the Province of Ontario be encouraged to consult with the following groups to ensure that regulatory modernization supports both user safety and accessibility goals: a. Ontario Association of Professional Audiology Clinics (OAPAC) b. Speech-Language & Audiology Canada (SAC)\ c. The College of Audiologists and Speech-Language Pathologists of Ontario (CASLPO) d. Accessibility organizations e. Seniors' organizations and disability advocacy groups f. Technology manufacturers, including Apple, and g. Consumer protection and public health stakeholders 4. That the Province of Ontario be encouraged to work with technology manufacturers, municipalities, public-sector organizations, and accessibility stakeholders to support the implementation of modern assistive listening standards such as Auracast, enabling greater accessibility in public and private environments. 5. That a copy of this motion be circulated to Premier Doug Ford, Minister of Health Sylvia Jones, Minister of Seniors and Accessibility Raymond Cho, Associate Minister of Mental Health and Addictions Vijay Thanigasalam, Ajax MP Jennifer McKelvie, All Federal MP's of Durham Region Municipalities, Ajax MPP Rob Cerjanec, All Provincial MPP's of Durham Region, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), Ontario Association of Professional Audiology Clinics (OAPAC), Speech-Language & Audiology Canada (SAC), College of Audiologists and Speech-Language Pathologists of Ontario (CASLPO), and Durham Region Municipal Accessibility Advisory Committees.

Whereas Diwali, widely recognized as the Festival of Lights, will be observed on November 8th, 2026, and is a significant festival celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, Tamil, Indo Caribbean and some Buddhist communities as a time of reflection, renewal, community and the triumph of light over darkness; and, Whereas Durham Diwali Festival (DDF) is an organization comprised of representatives from the Hindu Community Centre of Durham, the Hindu Federation, the Hindu Affinity Network of Durham and many other community partners; and, Whereas the DDF, with the approval of the Durham District School Board through Community Use of Schools, is hosting a Festival of Lights event on October 24, 2026, at J. Clarke Richardson Collegiate, with the fireworks to be lit from a private property at 250 Rossland Road East; and Whereas the Town's Fireworks By-law 43-2025 Section 11.1 states that “permits issued pursuant to this By-law shall be valid, subject to the other provisions of the By-law, for a period of time not to exceed seven (7) days immediately preceding the Statutory or Cultural Holidays known as the Lunar New Year, Eid al-Fitr, Victoria Day, Canada Day, and Diwali”. Therefore, be it resolved: 1. That Council approve an exemption to Fireworks By-law 43-2025 to permit fireworks as part of the Festival of Lights event on October 24, 2026, at J. Clarke Richardson Collegiate; and 2. That Durham Diwali Festival (DDF) be requested to submit an application for a display fireworks permit and all required supporting documentation to the Town no later than October 19, 2026; and 3. That, subject to all applicable By-law requirements and Ajax Fire and Emergency Services approval, public notice of the fireworks display be provided through the Town's website and social media channels.
That By-law 87-2026 be approved.
That By-laws 88-2026 to 95-2026 be approved.
